newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria raises tobacco purchase prices by 25 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria raises tobacco purchase prices by 25 pct.

text.p: Bulgaria's government raised purchase prices for tobacco from this year' crop by an average of 25 percent in a bid to stimulate local tobacco growers, the Agriculture Minister said on Thursday.
"The government set new tobacco purchase prices, which are 25 percent higher on the average in German mark denomination from last year's prices ," Ventzislav Varbanov told repoters.

The local lev currency was pegged at 1,000 to the mark from July 1 under an IMF-prescribed fixed exchange rate mechanism, a currency board, designed to restore confidence in Bulgaria's financial system.
The new prices of Virginia tobacco vary between 1.07-2.78 marks per kilogramme depending on quality compared to 0.78- 2.25 marks for tobacco from 1996 crop.
Prices of Barley tobacco will range between 1.08-1.99 marks per kilogramme, up from previous 0.78-1.62 mark per kilogramme, Varbanov said.

Prime Minister Ivan Kostov said on Tuesday Bulgaria expected its tobacco output to double to 80,000 tonnes this year, compared to 39,790 tonnes in 1996 and a record low output of 25,000 tonnes two years ago.
"The new prices are favourable for producers and they might be kept unchange in the future," Varbanov said.
Local tobacco purchase prices are updated semi-annually in line with inflation -- in mid-July and mid-October. Private growers also qualify for additional payments from the state Tobacco Fund.
Monthly consumer price inflation for June was 0.8 percent and year on year inflation was 1,526 percent last month. Cumulative inflation for the first six months of this year was 484 percent.
